newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar closes weaker, trade remains active.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar closes weaker, trade remains active.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed weaker on Friday on U.S. dollar short-covering and dealers said the market's volatile movements after a sharp three-day appreciation may have come to an end.
The local unit ended at T$27.391 to the U.S. dollar against Thursday's T$27.338 finish. Turnover was an active US$435 million, compared with Thursday's US$357 million.

The U.S. dollar's strength against the yen in Tokyo's afternoon halted the Taiwan dollar's rise and active short-covering on the U.S. currency pulled the Taiwan dollar to as low as T$27.405 at one stage.
"Recent sharp movements in the exchange rate were mainly triggered by strong expectations the Taiwan dollar would go up," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
Expectations were triggered by traditionally high Taiwan dollar demand before the Chinese new year, which falls on February 7, dealers said.
"Many investors took the chance to trade actively but they should trade more rationally next week," the dealer said.
Said a second dealer: "There are not too many fundamentals for the Taiwan dollar to rise sharply. Investors will soon realise that."
Though the central bank had said it would fully respect market forces, many dealers kept their doubts.
"The central bank can allow some movements but not big movements in the market," said the first dealer.

The central bank keeps a policy of maintaining a relatively stable foreign exchange rate but has taken what it implied was a hands-off policy, saying recent active movements were normal as well as beneficial to the market.
Though the Taiwan dollar was expected to remain firm before the lunar new year, no major appreciation was likely, dealers said. It was likely to move around T$27.35 in the near term.
Speaking after the market close, central bank vice governor Liang Cheng-chin repeated the bank's view that what happened during the week was seen as normal.
"Movements in the foreign exchange market reflect international and domestic trends. Appreciation and depreciation are normal," Liang said.
Liang would not be drawn when asked whether the bank had intervened, merely restating the bank's pro-market policy.
"The central bank's monetary policy remains to respect market functions," Liang said.
